il-cook-2026-cps-board-president-revulur.name: Sendhil Revuluri
il-cook-2026-cps-board-president-revulur.bio: CPS parent, former teacher, and former Vice President of the Chicago Board of Education.

positions.stance: Would align the board's work around clear goals for student success and "fight for strong instruction in every classroom."
Wants families in every neighborhood to understand the board's work and to listen to all Chicagoans, "not just the insiders."
Supports passing "realistic, sustainable budgets" with forward-looking funding aligned with top priorities for student learning.

il-cook-2026-cps-board-president-domingu.name: Hilario Dominguez
il-cook-2026-cps-board-president-domingu.bio: Former Chicago Public Schools teacher and CPS graduate.

positions.stance: Supports free full-day pre-K for every Chicago family starting at age three instead of four.
Says school meals "should be a cornerstone of student health, academic success, and community investment" and the district can serve better food while saving money.
Says the state owes Chicago schools $2 billion and pledges to pursue full funding for sustainable community schools.
Wants CPS to connect students to good jobs and launch life-long careers through youth jobs and career pathways.
Supports a three-year moratorium on the use of generative artificial intelligence in Chicago public schools.
Says district meeting minutes are hard to access and that resources for informed voting should be readily available to the public.
Says supervisors should be reminded "they are an elected body accountable to the people" and he would check their excesses or publicize them.
Says respect for property rights entails "an obligation not to degrade the property of others" through soil erosion.

nc-wake-2026-soil-water-farrell-elizabet.name: Beth Pugh Farrell
nc-wake-2026-soil-water-farrell-elizabet.bio: Wake Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor since 2022 and current Board Chair.

positions.stance: Says ensuring local farms have the conservation tools they need to stay in production is vital to local and regional food security.
Supports conserving natural resources such as soil, water, forests, and wildlife.
Says collaboration is essential to enhance voluntary rural and urban soil and water conservation efforts "from Apex to Zebulon."
Supports outreach programs such as Envirothon, the annual Poster Contest, and workshops to educate youth, families and teachers about conservation.
Would strengthen partnerships and conservation programs that help farmers stay productive and profitable while encouraging innovation in local food production.
Would encourage partnerships and programs that help landowners see agriculture as "a viable long-term investment."
Supports practical conservation practices that improve water quality, reduce erosion, strengthen watersheds, and increase resilience to flooding.
Would strengthen relationships with landowners, businesses, schools and others; says solutions are "built through collaboration—not regulation."

nc-wake-2026-soil-water-lewis-brian.name: Brian K. Lewis
nc-wake-2026-soil-water-lewis-brian.bio: Small-scale farmer in Wake County, U.S. Navy veteran, and former Broward (Florida) Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor.

positions.stance: Supports protecting lakes, streams, and riparian zones and managing stormwater runoff to protect Wake County's water supply.
Supports urban farming initiatives to make local agricultural abundance accessible to all communities and help eliminate food deserts.
Supports public outreach and making up-to-date soil and water data and best techniques accessible.
Would foster cooperation with soil and water supervisors in other counties on shared watersheds.
Says hemp and cannabis legalization "should be a priority," citing agricultural revenue, criminal justice and the opioid epidemic.

nc-wake-2026-soil-water-krop-samantha.name: Samantha Krop
nc-wake-2026-soil-water-krop-samantha.bio: Environmental advocate and educator with over a decade of experience working to protect clean water and conserve forests.

positions.stance: Would protect drinking water at its source by conserving forests, wetlands, and riparian buffers that safeguard Falls Lake and Jordan Lake.
Would expand nature-based solutions such as stream restoration, wetland protection, reforestation, and green stormwater infrastructure.
Says "conservation and environmental justice go hand in hand" and supports investing in natural infrastructure in communities most burdened.

nc-wake-2026-soil-water-grant-cincilla.name: Cece Grant
nc-wake-2026-soil-water-grant-cincilla.bio: Government affairs and public policy professional with service on Capitol Hill and in the Obama Administration.

positions.stance: Would make the Soil and Water Conservation District more visible so more residents know the resources available to them.
Would protect working farms and preserve agricultural land as Wake County grows.
Would expand access to conservation programs that help homeowners and communities solve real-world problems.
Supports practical solutions that improve water quality, reduce erosion, and strengthen resilience to flooding.
Would partner with schools, nonprofits, businesses, and local governments to encourage stewardship across Wake County.

nc-wake-2026-raleigh-mayor-cowell-janet.name: Janet Cowell
nc-wake-2026-raleigh-mayor-cowell-janet.bio: Mayor of Raleigh since December 2024; former Raleigh City Councilor, North Carolina State Senator, State Treasurer, and Dix Park Conservancy CEO.

positions.stance: Would diversify housing options citywide, invest in infrastructure, and work with nonprofits like DHIC to build affordable housing.
Would implement "a forward-looking rezoning plan" built on public input and comprehensive review.
Would support police with staffing, equipment and pay, and partner with the state and county so mental health providers can respond to non-criminal crises.
Would protect the tree canopy and open spaces, reduce city emissions, and address resiliency after natural disasters.

nc-wake-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-br.name: Joshua Bradley
nc-wake-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-br.bio: Hospitality industry worker for over twenty years.

positions.stance: Says "housing is a human right" and housing must be affordable to people earning minimum income.
Says the city must address historical inequities, with a focus on Black, brown, and Indigenous communities.
Supports labor unions and city policies that improve working conditions for city workers.
Says Raleigh should lead in mitigating greenhouse gas production and prioritize environmental impacts in all decision making.
Lists non-discrimination and community inclusion as one of five fundamental policy commitments.

nc-wake-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-fo.name: Ms. Stormie Denise Forte
nc-wake-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-fo.bio: Raleigh City Council member and licensed attorney.

positions.stance: Working to ensure all Raleigh citizens, especially those in disenfranchised communities, have access to affordable housing.
Supports improving community mobility both in and outside of the beltline.
Working to ensure the stability of the city's infrastructure matches its growth.
Would partner with grassroots organizations to help promote growth and development of Raleigh small businesses.

nc-wake-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-ri.name: Clark Rinehart
nc-wake-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-ri.bio: Former pastor and small business and community builder in Raleigh.

positions.stance: Supports building more housing of more types and price points across the whole city, with tools to reduce displacement.
Supports "efficient, reliable, affordable multimodal transportation," including more frequent transit and safer crossings.
Would properly staff, pay, and support first responders, paired with transparency, accountability, and de-escalation training.
Would reduce unnecessary friction between small businesses and city processes and help entrepreneurs navigate city resources.

nc-wake-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-si.name: Sana Siddiqui
nc-wake-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-si.bio: Small business owner, NC State engineering alum, and member of multiple Raleigh advisory boards.

positions.stance: Would reduce unnecessary friction for small businesses, improve access to clear information, and support policies that help them stay in business.
Supports expanding housing options with affordability at the center, protecting long-time residents from displacement, and planning growth with infrastructure.
Supports city staff and frontline workers, saying it leads to better service and a government that works reliably.
Says residents "deserve to see how their input mattered" and supports earlier outreach and clear follow-up.
Would end the dumping of harmful materials in Wayne County and have the county budget better support preventative care.
Would advocate for better curricula through Wayne RESA and "higher teacher wages."
Says "I will lower the cost of living" to retain residents and attract new neighbors.
Believes government "should be fiscally responsible and deliver high quality service" and protect citizens from new hazards.
Pledges to "considerably lower the property taxes for everyone in Wayne County" and halt foreclosures.

wa-king-2026-prosecutor-manion-leesa.name: Leesa Manion
wa-king-2026-prosecutor-manion-leesa.bio: King County Prosecuting Attorney since 2023; previously Chief of Staff of the King County Prosecuting Attorney's Office for 15 years.

positions.stance: Cites establishing Gender-Based Violence & Prevention and Economic Crimes & Wage Theft divisions to address these priorities.
Cites adding dedicated staffing and increasing criminal filings to combat retail crime and organized retail theft.
Cites working with law enforcement to file hundreds of charges annually against people dealing fentanyl and methamphetamine.
Cites renewing the office's commitment to Drug Court as an alternative for nonviolent offenders.
Cites expanding capacity to address hate crimes, including advancing legislative reforms.

wa-king-2026-assessor-foxcurran-rob.name: Rob Foxcurran
wa-king-2026-assessor-foxcurran-rob.bio: Appraiser for the City of Seattle and Hearing Examiner on the King County Board of Appeals and Equalization.

positions.stance: Would push for a universal homestead exemption, expanded relief programs, and monthly payment options.
Supports building a system that ties property taxes to income "so no one is taxed out of their neighborhood."
Would work to correct the commercial property tax imbalance and ensure "the wealthiest corporations pay their fair share."
Would identify surplus land and coordinate across agencies to help build more affordable housing.
Would ensure personal property taxes are assessed accurately so entrepreneurs "pay what they owe, no more and no less."
